page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c5.8xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on the x86_64 architecture and managed via the KVM hypervisor. It is powered by an Intel Xeon 8163 processor clocked at 2.5 GHz, delivering 32 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 16 physical cores with 2 threads per core. The processor features 32 KB of L1 data cache per core, 1.0 MB of L2 cache per core, and a 33 MB shared L3 cache, alongside hardware support for AVX, AVX-512F, and AES instructions. The system includes 64.0 GB of RAM, adhering strictly to a 1:2 memory-to-vCPU ratio with 2.0 GB of memory per core. It lacks integrated local storage, requiring network-attached storage volumes, and features no GPU acceleration. A baseline network bandwidth of 10 Gbps is standard.

Benchmark results demonstrate a clear split between single-threaded and multi-threaded throughput. Single-core evaluations reflect lower relative performance, as indicated by a stress-ng single-core score of 1109.09, a Geekbench single-core score of 958.0, and a gzip compression throughput of 19.13 GB/sec, placing it in lower performance tiers. However, multi-threaded tasks scale comfortably into mid-tier cloud benchmarks. It achieves a Geekbench multi-core score of 8420.0, a stress-ng multi-core result of 23532.01, and a PassMark CPU score of 23029.39. Parallel operations such as bzip3 multi-threaded decompression reached 104.04 GB/sec, and clang software compilation produced an 18451.0 Geekbench rating.

Data handling and memory metrics align with its compute-oriented architecture. Large-block memory bandwidth is measured at 98.09 GB/sec for reads and 43.54 GB/sec for writes, alongside a small-block cached read throughput of 1311.89 GB/sec. Application testing demonstrates 23.06 million operations per second in Redis SET workloads and 14.01 GB/sec in static web serving throughput. On smaller LLM tasks, prompt processing yields 1372.31 tokens/sec with the 135M model and 40.44 tokens/sec on the 7B model, though text generation speeds are constrained by the absence of specialized accelerators and moderate single-thread execution rates.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the ecs.c5.8xlarge delivers balanced multithreaded capacity for standard enterprise CPU demands without the premium overhead associated with GPU accelerators or high memory ratios. Tradeoffs include modest single-core execution speed and the operational dependence on external persistent storage. This hardware profile is appropriate for multi-threaded build environments, software compilation via CI/CD pipelines, containerized application clusters, batch processing, and horizontally scaled web serving.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c5.8xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual server configured with 32 dedicated vCPUs and 16 physical cores on an Intel Xeon 8163 processor running at 2.5 GHz. Built on x86_64 architecture with KVM virtualization, it includes 64.0 GB of system memory, matching a 1:2 compute-to-RAM ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. The instance does not include local disk storage or hardware GPU accelerators, relying on a 10 Gbps baseline network interface. Benchmark results indicate moderate multi-core capabilities, achieving a Geekbench multi-core rating of 8420.0, a PassMark CPU score of 23029.39, and a multi-threaded bzip3 decompression rate of 104.04 GB/sec. Single-core execution reflects lower performance tiers across synthetic benchmarks. The instance suits horizontally scaled, multi-threaded workloads such as code compilation, CI/CD workers, batch compute operations, and medium-scale web serving environments.
